Trump Hails Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan Defense Pact; India Assesses Security

U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed a newly signed defense pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, calling it a "big, bold, first step" and a sign that "the Middle East is coming together." The agreement, referred to as the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, has prompted India to weigh its national security implications. Some outlets described the pact as an "Islamic NATO." Meanwhile, other reports indicate that nine Muslim nations, including Egypt, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Turkey, Pakistan, and Indonesia, condemned Israel's rejection of Trump's Gaza plan, stating it could weaken efforts to end the war.
